_comment: Permission rules the secret guard owns. These cover the Read and Edit tools, whose output
a PreToolUse hook cannot filter — the hook can rewrite a shell read into a redacted read,
but it cannot redact what a file-reading tool returns, so those paths are denied outright.
TWO ANCHORS, BOTH REQUIRED. This was originally shipped with only the '**/' form, on the
belief that a '//'-prefixed twin was accumulated duplication. It is not, and the mistake
**/x    gitignore semantics, anchored at the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY. Matches x at any
depth at or under it. Does NOT match a sibling project, a parent directory, or a
//x     anchored at the FILESYSTEM ROOT. This is the only form that covers an absolute
path outside the workspace, or a relative path that escapes it via '..'.
A single leading slash is neither: it anchors at the settings source, so '/etc/hosts' does
not name the system hosts file. It has to be '//etc/hosts'.
'~/' anchors at the home directory and is already absolute in effect, so those entries need
read: redaction would be meaningful but the tool cannot be intercepted, so deny.
edit: raw key material and credential stores, where an edit is a rewrite of a secret.
